summary: Phase F10.3 Payment Mismatch -> Raise Inquiry frontend flow VERIFIED end-to-end via Playwright on mobile viewport (390x844). 5/5 UI tests pass. On shipment EG350860354IN (id=5e2559...) whose persisted import_validation_alerts contains a payment-field entry (currently field=amount, existing=719, imported=999), the red inline 'Raise Inquiry' button renders inside the alert row. Tapping it (1) expands the collapsed India Post Complaint section and (2) seeds the Description with the EXACT string 'Payment discrepancy found. Expected: ₹719, Received: ₹999. Please clarify the difference.'. Draft-safety guard verified: after typing operator text and re-tapping Raise Inquiry, description is NOT overwritten. Regression: a different shipment with no import_validation_alerts renders zero Raise Inquiry buttons. Column labels honour the field-type swap: for field='amount' the labels remain Booked/Imported (only cod_amount rows swap to Expected/Received per the spec).
critical_code_review_comments: State bump uses a plain string setInquiryPrefill(msg) — if the operator taps the same alert twice in a row and the string is byte-identical, React will not fire the useEffect the second time because the prop reference did not change. The inline comment at line 678-680 acknowledges this and mentions a 'nonce' but the code does not actually append one. Non-blocking for the primary happy-path (first tap always triggers), but worth appending a stable nonce (e.g. Date.now() or a monotonic counter) if the product wants a 'reset draft' path via re-tap. Currently the draft-safety guard would swallow that anyway, so behaviour is correct as-shipped.
shipment-details/[id].tsx is now 1764 lines. Splitting IndiaPostComplaintSection (~600 lines) into a sibling file would bring the parent under the 700-line guideline. Non-blocking.

Alert values are rendered via String(a.existing ?? '') — the underlying Mongo field is a float (e.g. 719.0). Currently JSON marshaling produces `719` in the payload we tested, so the exact-string spec passes. If backend ever serialises as `719.0`, the prefill would read '₹719.0' and drift from the spec. Backend behaviour is stable today; flagged only for future awareness.
